purpose: Define a coherent broad mathematics curriculum from foundational numeracy through advanced undergraduate-level capabilities, with applied pathways. This is a scope and sequencing contract, not proof that all teaching content has been authored.

strands.title: Numeracy and number systems
strands.scope: Place value; integers; rational and irrational numbers; real number properties; divisibility; primes; factors and multiples; fractions; decimals; percentages; ratio; rates; estimation; significant figures; scientific notation.

strands.title: Algebra and symbolic reasoning
strands.scope: Variables; expressions; equivalence; equations; inequalities; rearrangement; identities; polynomials; factoring; rational expressions; radicals; complex numbers; systems; matrices; modelling.

strands.title: Functions and mathematical modelling
strands.scope: Relations; domain/range; function notation; transformations; inverses; composition; linear, quadratic, polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, piecewise and periodic models; model fit and limitations.

strands.title: Geometry and spatial reasoning
strands.scope: Euclidean geometry; angles; triangles; congruence; similarity; polygons; circles; constructions; coordinate geometry; vectors; transformations; proof; perimeter, area, surface area, volume; measurement uncertainty.

strands.title: Trigonometry
strands.scope: Right-triangle ratios; radians; unit circle; identities; graphs; inverse trig; equations; sine/cosine rules; bearings; vectors; periodic applications.

strands.title: Sequences, series and discrete patterns
strands.scope: Arithmetic/geometric sequences; recursive definitions; summation; finite/infinite series; convergence basics; recurrence; induction; binomial theorem; growth patterns.

strands.title: Probability and combinatorics
strands.scope: Sample spaces; counting principles; permutations; combinations; conditional probability; independence; Bayes rule; random variables; expectation; distributions; simulation.

strands.title: Statistics and data reasoning
strands.scope: Data types; sampling; bias; visualisation; centre/spread; quantiles; outliers; probability models; estimation; confidence intervals; hypothesis tests; correlation/regression; causal limits.

strands.title: Calculus and continuous change
strands.scope: Limits; continuity; derivatives; rules; implicit differentiation; optimisation; related rates; integrals; accumulation; fundamental theorem; techniques; differential equations; multivariable introduction.

strands.title: Linear algebra
strands.scope: Vectors; matrices; linear systems; row reduction; span; linear independence; subspaces; basis/dimension; linear transformations; determinants; eigenvalues/eigenvectors; least squares.

strands.title: Discrete mathematics and logic
strands.scope: Propositional/predicate logic; sets; relations; functions; proof methods; induction; recursion; graph theory; trees; combinatorics; Boolean algebra; modular arithmetic; algorithmic complexity foundations.

strands.title: Number theory
strands.scope: Divisibility; primes; gcd/lcm; Euclidean algorithm; congruences; modular arithmetic; Diophantine equations; elementary cryptographic mathematics and limitations.

strands.title: Numerical and computational mathematics
strands.scope: Approximation; error; floating-point representation; numerical root finding; interpolation; numerical differentiation/integration; iterative methods; stability; reproducibility; computational verification.

strands.title: Optimisation and operations research
strands.scope: Objective functions; constraints; feasible regions; linear programming; integer programming concepts; networks; scheduling; decision analysis; sensitivity and uncertainty.

strands.title: Mathematical modelling and applied quantitative reasoning
strands.scope: Dimensional analysis; proportional models; scaling; rates; finance mathematics; physical models; uncertainty; sensitivity; validation; ethical communication of quantitative conclusions.

strands.title: Mathematical communication and proof
strands.scope: Definitions; conjectures; counterexamples; direct proof; contradiction; contrapositive; induction; proof critique; notation; mathematical writing; diagram and data argument.

strands.title: Foundations of mathematical practice
strands.scope: Problem formulation; strategy selection; estimation; checking; tool selection; calculator/spreadsheet/CAS use; reproducible working; mathematical history and context; responsible use of computational outputs.

pathways.title: Core quantitative literacy
pathways.outcome: Interpret quantities, calculate reliably, model common relationships, evaluate data claims and communicate justified conclusions.

pathways.title: STEM mathematics
pathways.outcome: Use algebra, functions, geometry, trigonometry, calculus, linear algebra and numerical methods in scientific and engineering contexts.

pathways.title: Computing and discrete mathematics
pathways.outcome: Reason about discrete structures, algorithms, probability, modular arithmetic and computational representations.

pathways.title: Statistics and data science foundations
pathways.outcome: Collect, analyse, model and communicate data while accounting for uncertainty, bias and causal limitations.

pathways.title: Finance, optimisation and decision mathematics
pathways.outcome: Compare quantitative options, model constraints and evaluate uncertainty without confusing models with guarantees.

completion_policy.scope_definition: A strand is not complete when its title and scope exist. It requires sequenced learning units, specific objectives, accurate teaching, worked examples, practice with solutions, misconception feedback, assessments/rubrics, applied transfer, resources with provenance, retention design, prerequisites and review status.
completion_policy.no_false_completion: Do not mark a strand or discipline approved when any required component is missing or when external review is pending.
completion_policy.level_ceiling: The v1.0 baseline should define a coherent path to functional competence and clearly marked advanced branches; it must not imply mastery of every specialised research subfield.
